p.src: A density matrix first appears as the natural description of incomplete preparation: a quantum system has been prepared, but we do not know exactly how. Entanglement gives the same mathematical object a deeper role. Even when the state of a composite system is known completely, a subsystem generally has no state vector of its own. Its reduced density matrix contains everything that can be predicted locally. We shall derive that statement in components, test it on two spin states, and use entropy to distinguish product states from entangled ones. Then we shall turn to a second question: how a quantum state changes with time. Preservation of inner products will lead to unitarity, a Hermitian generator, and the Schrödinger equation.

ja: 密度行列は、まず不完全な準備の自然な記述として現れる。すなわち、量子系は準備されているが、どのように準備されたかを正確には知らないのである。エンタングルメントは、同じ数学的対象にさらに深い役割を与える。複合系の状態が完全に知られている場合でも、一般に部分系はそれ自身の状態ベクトルを持たない。その縮約密度行列は、局所的に予測できるすべてを含んでいる。この主張を成分で導き、二つのスピン状態で検証し、エントロピーを用いて積状態とエンタングルした状態を区別する。次に第二の問い、すなわち量子状態が時間とともにどのように変化するかに移る。内積の保存はユニタリ性、エルミート生成子、そしてSchrödinger方程式へと導く。
zh: 密度矩阵最初是作为不完全制备的自然描述而出现的：一个量子系统已被制备，但我们并不确切知道它是如何被制备的。纠缠赋予同一个数学对象以更深刻的角色。即便复合系统的态被完全知晓，其子系统一般也没有属于自己的态矢量。它的约化密度矩阵包含了所有能在局部被预测的信息。我们将用分量推导这一论断，在两个自旋态上检验它，并用熵来区分乘积态与纠缠态。随后我们将转向第二个问题：量子态如何随时间变化。内积的保持将引出幺正性、厄米生成元以及Schrödinger方程。

p.src: Suppose an electron has been placed in a strong magnetic field and allowed to align with it. Someone else chose the field direction and prepared the electron, but did not tell us the direction. The spin may therefore be in a perfectly definite pure state even though we do not know which state it is. We may know a probability distribution over possible preparations, or we may know nothing at all. A density matrix $\rho$ is the quantum description of precisely this kind of incomplete information.

p.src:
For a classical probability distribution $\{p_i\}$, define $S=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i,$ with $0\log 0$ understood as its limiting value $0$. If one probability equals $1$ and all others vanish, then $S=0$: the state is known. If all $n$ possibilities are equally likely, $p_i=\frac{1}{n},
\qquad
S=-n\left(\frac{1}{n}\log\frac{1}{n}\right)=\log n.$ Thus entropy grows as the probability distribution spreads over more significant possibilities. Roughly, $e^S$ is the effective number of comparably weighted states when natural logarithms are used.

When does $\rho_A$ remain pure? The answer is that the wave function must factorize: $\psi(a,b)=\phi(a)\chi(b).$ Assume $\phi$ and $\chi$ are separately normalized. Substitution into the reduced density matrix gives $\begin{aligned}\rho_A(a,a')
&=\sum_b\phi(a)\chi(b)\phi^*(a')\chi^*(b) \\
&=\phi(a)\phi^*(a')\sum_b|\chi(b)|^2 \\
&=\phi(a)\phi^*(a').\end{aligned}$ Thus $\rho_A=\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}.$ It has one eigenvalue $1$, all remaining eigenvalues $0$, and zero entropy.

p.src:
Let $\epsilon$ be a very small time interval. Since $U(0)=I$, write the first-order expansion $U(\epsilon)=I-i\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2).$ The minus sign and the factor of $i$ are convenient conventions. Taking the Hermitian conjugate gives $U^\dagger(\epsilon)
=I+i\epsilon h^\dagger+O(\epsilon^2).$ Unitarity then requires $\begin{aligned}I
&=U^\dagger(\epsilon)U(\epsilon) \\
&=\left(I+i\epsilon h^\dagger\right)
\left(I-i\epsilon h\right)+O(\epsilon^2) \\
&=I+i\epsilon(h^\dagger-h)+O(\epsilon^2).\end{aligned}$ The first-order term must vanish: $\boxed{h^\dagger=h}.$ The infinitesimal generator is Hermitian.
